title: Dual coefficient system 𝒦*: F ↦ κ_F* (geometrization of (E3))
body_html:
Dual coefficient system $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \kappa_\mathcal{F}^*$

Goal: turn the abstract hypothesis (E3) into a geometric structure on $\BSigma$.

Setup

For two facets with $\mathcal{E} \subseteq \overline{\mathcal{F}}$, (E3) gives the isomorphism $$\iota_{\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}} : \cInd_{\hat K_\mathcal{F}}^{\hat K_\mathcal{F} K_{\mathcal{E}, 0+}} \kappa_\mathcal{F} \;\xrightarrow{\;\cong\;}\; \kappa_\mathcal{E}|_{\hat K_\mathcal{F} K_{\mathcal{E}, 0+}},$$ realized as $$\iota_{\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}}(f) = \sum_{[g] \in \hat K_\mathcal{F} K_{\mathcal{E}, 0+} / \hat K_\mathcal{F}} g \cdot r^\mathcal{F}_\mathcal{E}(f(g)).$$

In the standard "functions on $B$ with $f(ba) = a^{-1} f(b)$" realization of $\cInd$, we have $\mathrm{proj}_e \circ i_e = \id$. Define $$\mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F}} := \mathrm{proj}_e \circ \iota_{\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}}^{-1} : \kappa_\mathcal{E} \to \kappa_\mathcal{F}.$$

Key property: $\mathrm{proj}{\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F}} \circ r^\mathcal{F}\mathcal{E} = \id_{\kappa_\mathcal{F}}$. Its kernel is $\sum_{[g] \ne [e]} g \cdot \mathrm{Im}(r^\mathcal{F}_\mathcal{E})$ in the decomposition $\kappa_\mathcal{E} = \bigoplus_{[g]} g \cdot \mathrm{Im}(r^\mathcal{F}_\mathcal{E})$.

The theorem

Theorem (Sheaf7 §8). The assignment $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \kappa_\mathcal{F}^*$ with transition map $(r^){\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}} := (\mathrm{proj}{\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F}})^ : \kappa^_\mathcal{F} \to \kappa^_\mathcal{E}$ for $\mathcal{E} \subseteq \overline{\mathcal{F}}$ defines a $G$-equivariant coefficient system of $R$-modules on $\BSigma$.
proof_html: Functoriality reduces to $\mathrm{proj}{\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F}} \circ \mathrm{proj}{\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{E}} = \mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{F}}$ for $\mathcal{D} \le \mathcal{E} \le \mathcal{F}$. Since each projection is characterized by its kernel, this follows from the fibration $$K_{\mathcal{E}, 0+} / (K_{\mathcal{F}, 0+} \cap K_{\mathcal{E}, 0+}) \hookrightarrow K_{\mathcal{F}, 0+} K_{\mathcal{D}, 0+} / K_{\mathcal{F}, 0+} \twoheadrightarrow K_{\mathcal{E}, 0+} K_{\mathcal{D}, 0+} / K_{\mathcal{E}, 0+}.$$ The $G$-action is $r_{g, \mathcal{F}} \circ c(g)$. $\square$
